question: Should OpenClaw accept Android device-control, ADB-style access, or dynamic code execution from connected Android nodes, and should those capabilities be Android-specific commands or generic node-advertised tools?
rationale: The remaining requests change phone authority, sensitive-data access, and model-visible execution boundaries, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product and security model.

options.title: Split and gate Android authority
options.body: Implement only narrow Android device-control commands after explicit permission UX and policy review, while deferring ADB and dynamic execution until the generic node-tool trust model is accepted.

options.title: Route through node-hosted tools
options.body: Use the generic node-registered/node-hosted tool design first, then let Android expose approved descriptors through that contract.

options.title: Keep high-power execution external
options.body: Decline ADB and dynamic Android code execution in core for now and require an external plugin, ClawHub package, or app-specific fork for that authority.

recommendation.title: Split and gate Android authority
recommendation.body: Implement only narrow Android device-control commands after explicit permission UX and policy review, while deferring ADB and dynamic execution until the generic node-tool trust model is accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: The closest current decision-owner signal is the adjacent node-hosted plugin tools work and generic node-to-model security boundary.
